page: Amazon Web Services x1e.16xlarge is a dedicated memory-optimized instance engineered for enterprise workloads requiring extensive in-memory footprint. It runs on the Xen hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture and is driven by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 45 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 1952.0 GB, yielding 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 1920 GB SSD, and network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear trade-off between memory footprint and individual core throughput. Due to the older Haswell generation processor, single-core processing scores in the bottom 10 percent, with Geekbench recording 846.0 and stress-ng reaching 738.09. Conversely, multithreaded operations benefit from all 64 vCPUs, yielding average scores in PassMark CPU (30064.31), stress-ng multi-core (29107.26), and Clang software compilation (21740.0). In-memory database processing remains solid, with Redis SET throughput achieving 31.17 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x1e.16xlarge allocates a massive RAM density relative to its compute power, making it appropriate primarily when memory capacity is the binding constraint rather than raw compute speed. Typical fit includes large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, enterprise caching layers, big data memory caches, and memory-bound transactional or analytical database systems.
description: Amazon Web Services x1e.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Designed for memory-bound workloads, it provides an exceptional 1952.0 GB of RAM alongside 1920 GB of local SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark metrics highlight modest single-threaded performance offset by balanced multithreaded capacity, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 7914.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 30064.31. In-memory throughput is substantiated by 31.17 million Redis SET operations per second and 112.99 GB/sec uncached large-block memory read bandwidth. Due to its high RAM-to-vCPU allocation of 30.5 GB per vCPU, x1e.16xlarge serves as a specialized compute platform for large in-memory enterprise databases, extensive caching layers, and high-footprint data processing applications where memory footprint supersedes raw clock frequencies.
